summary: Short mṭ-/moṭ-/məṭy- forms are filed here following the supplied entry; amṭele and Mṭele alternate in MAC Besim History of Bsorino/33, and 60/311 alternates mṭəlli with mamṭəlli. This supports a morphological continuum with mṭy 1 III, not a newly separate lexical meaning.

Theme, source m-, goal l-/gab-, and recipient suffixes co-occur; mṭé-la-le distinguishes female agent and male recipient. In I.2 the arranging parent may procure a spouse for another person, as already shown by the editors’ examples.

ko-Preterit has completed/result uses; the narrative komṭele in MAC NE Ditin Hazar/14 could alternatively be contracted Infectum plus recipient -le, so it is not selected as decisive form evidence. Habitual Infectum-wa occurs in practical descriptions and autobiographical recollection.

The supplied parsed entry has four Preterit 2 examples, not a sense-4 group: the repeated reader numbering complaint is unsupported and no renumbering is made. Counts after moving 36/135: Preterit 1 has two existing examples; Infectum 1 three; Imperativ 1 four.

Routine counts (not additional decision lines): Preterit 1 162; Infectum 1 103; Imperativ 1 38; Infectum-wa 1 8; Infectum 2 6; Preterit 2 1. These support frequency only, and are not box example counts.

Plain t spellings gmotatte and mətyole are retained in decisions; the separately listed mty entry cannot be merged on spelling alone. The existing intercession phrase is not added again; its FA 54 reference and the supplied /62 numbering may belong to different systems.

Batch 2 retains all earlier numbered senses and decisions except explicitly broadening the blow collocation gloss and aligning bride-procurement tokens with the existing son-beneficiary examples. New numbered senses are I.3 offspring production and I.4 reciprocal reconciliation.

69/34 has both bird parents as subject of gmoṭina farxe. It does not prove that the reproduction use is restricted to men; the queried male-only wording in the separate mṭy 1 III entry is not changed here.

Consent/willingness is expressed by qəm plus a coreferential possessor and sometimes a d-action clause (62/295,353;69/126;97/74,154). The related long form mamṭalle qīm dəṯṯe already appears under mṭy 1 III; constituent segmentation remains a question.
Additional same-verse short/full alternations occur in 64/220, 65/101, 75/341, 95/80 and 113/169,191; root allocation follows the supplied split without claiming new morphology.
The reduced pretext phrase in 103/36 corresponds to existing mṭy 1 III mamṭe/mamṭele ḥəǧǧe ʕal. Keep this as a cross-reference rather than a duplicate new idiom.

All eight supplied occurrences checked. No new numbered sense, stem, box, idiom or translated example is justified after cumulative round 1; this delta consists of evidence notes and editorial questions.

Lookup of mṭy 1 confirms III mamṭele/mamṭe and its reduced amṭ-/manṭ- examples. Overt causative candidates remain comparative evidence rather than creating a second III paradigm under the derived mṭy 2 entry. No other entry is edited.

Machine English does not decide agent/theme roles or whether habitual muṭewole/mṭele is Preterit-wa versus an Infectum-wa or recipient-suffixed form. Ambiguous forms are retained in decisions but not selected as published morphology examples.

The printed nominal ṭəmtiyo clearly occurs with a bringing event, women as theme and studio as goal; spelling and paradigm affiliation remain unresolved. The form lookup yielded possible consonantal matches only, not an attested nominal analysis.
How should mṭy 2 I and reduced mṭy 1 III be divided across dialects? In particular, is əmṭən (MAC NE Old lady and a bird/23) a reduced III form?

Confirm object/person segmentation in komṭinana, mṭannane, mṭūṭәle, məṭyówalle and the source forms with -lle. Does Mṭówalle in MAC NE Interview 2/27 contain -wa or a simple Preterit plural allomorph? It is withheld as a paradigm example.

Does mṭe ḏarbo ʕal- conventionally denote an opening to strike, aiming a blow, or both? The supplied narratives do not justify claiming that a blow was actually delivered.
Confirm conventional status and local morphology of the single l-darbo faith collocation and qanaʕa phrase. Does l-bol- allow an overt remembered theme?

The translation of 98/31 is flagged for alignment and adds Ali while allegedly omitting material; it is not quoted here. Confirm the correct verse/translation pairing before selecting that example.
Confirm the noun and possessive segmentation in qəm diḏ-/qəm iḏ- and its relationship to qīm dəṯṯe; is the willingness range uniform across 62/295,353;69/126;97/74,154?

summary: Event/abstract themes: bring sayfo upon a community, bring facts before a judge, bring timber into construction position. Record semantic extensions rather than proliferating senses.
Abstract/result-goal uses: direct a lot into cities (63/151), bring horns to blade shape (94/13), bring harm onto a head (104/34;113/65) or to recipients (113/187).
Anthropomorphic stork mate acquisition and counterfactual taking a mate parallel human wife acquisition; this is a participant extension of sense 2.
An inanimate ship is the carrier of its cargo, without a change from the transport meaning.
Jan confirms short mṭe-/mṭən- alongside amṭən- within one verse, continuing round 1's continuum with mṭy 1 III. Crops, greens and a property share are transport themes already covered.

Jan 3.36/1046 adds a Preterit-wa marriage candidate, with an overt wedding clause. The source -la and Karima may make her the agent of an object relative, whereas the machine English says he married Karima. Semantic support is retained without publishing a mismatched example.
